        "rationale": "Memory-only access tokens are XSS-resistant (no persistent readable storage) and the boot-refresh makes hard reloads seamless since the httpOnly cookie persists. Single-flight + Web Locks + BroadcastChannel is the standard answer to rotation-with-reuse-detection in multi-tab SPAs: it eliminates the benign-race family revocations the backend grace window only softens. Proactive renewal avoids latency spikes and thundering 401 retries. Keeping every fetch in apiClient.ts (per STRUCTURE) means the 401/retry/refresh logic exists exactly once.",
        "alternatives_rejected": "localStorage/sessionStorage tokens: XSS-exfiltratable, explicitly rejected. Access token in a cookie too: makes every API call CSRF-relevant instead of just /auth. Per-tab independent refresh without coordination: races rotation and logs users out under normal multi-tab use. Service-worker token broker: strictly more moving parts for the same isolation in a v1 SPA. Storing permissions in localStorage for instant boot: stale-permission UI and another sync problem — /auth/me is one cheap request.",
        "risks": "navigator.locks/BroadcastChannel need modern browsers — fine for v1 scope; a no-op fallback (per-tab single-flight only) keeps Safari/old engines working with the backend grace window absorbing the residual race. In-memory token dies on reload — by design; boot refresh restores it. Clock skew breaks proactive scheduling — harmless: the reactive 401 path is the safety net."
      },
      {
        "title": "Backend testing strategy (async fixtures, per-test DB copies, trigger tests on SQLite)",
        "decision": "pytest + pytest-asyncio with asyncio_mode=auto; HTTP tests use httpx.AsyncClient over ASGITransport(app) — no live server. Database isolation uses the TEMPLATE-COPY pattern, deliberately replacing the draft's SAVEPOINT/join-external-transaction approach, which breaks the moment code under test performs REAL commits — and ours does by design (idempotency's separate reservation transaction, run_in_uow commits, numbering claims): a session-scoped fixture builds ONE migrated template SQLite file via programmatic `alembic.command.upgrade(config, 'head')` (env.py's asyncio.run pattern works because the session fixture runs outside any event loop); a function-scoped fixture copies that file (shutil.copy, ~ms) into tmp_path, builds an aiosqlite engine on the copy with the connect-event `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`, and overrides the app's session dependency. Every test gets a fully migrated, trigger-bearing, fresh database where real commits are allowed and nothing leaks across tests. For the pg-marked subset in CI, a fixture creates a per-test database via `CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE atlas_test_template` from a once-migrated template database and drops it after — same semantics on Postgres. Fixtures in tests/conftest.py: `tenant_factory` provisions tenant + admin user + role with named permissions through the REAL provisioning service under system_context, returning a handle with tenant_id and an auth_headers(user) helper that performs a real login; `authed_client` composes it; `permissions_context` sets the current_permissions ContextVar for serializer-level masking tests; module fixtures live in tests/modules/<module>/conftest.py per STRUCTURE §6. DB-guard tests (tests/modules/finance/test_journal_db_guards.py etc.) deliberately use raw `session.execute(text(...))` to BYPASS the service layer — sanctioned because the CI grep gate banning text() is scoped to app/, not tests/ — asserting that UPDATE/DELETE on posted lines, unbalanced DRAFT→POSTED, closed-period posting, and audit UPDATE/DELETE all raise with the ATLAS_ tokens on SQLite, with the same tests re-run on Postgres via `-m pg`. The tenancy suite enumerates Base.registry.mappers (auto-covering new models); event-bus tests assert handler effects and rollback-on-handler-failure within one transaction; idempotency tests exercise the two-transaction reservation flow with real commits; determinism comes from explicit posting_date/anchor arguments in factories, not clock freezing.",
        "rationale": "The template-copy pattern is the single decision that makes everything else testable as designed: SAVEPOINT isolation silently converts the idempotency guard's real COMMIT into a savepoint release (changing the very semantics under test) and shares state when code opens a second session. File copies are milliseconds on SQLite and CREATE DATABASE TEMPLATE is fast on Postgres, so the cost is negligible while every test sees the exact schema migrations produce — triggers included, which is the whole point of asserting DB guards in CI. Factories going through real services means tenancy stamping, numbering, docflow, and audit are exercised by every test that touches data.",
        "alternatives_rejected": "SAVEPOINT/join-external-transaction per test (the draft): incompatible with real multi-transaction code paths and second sessions; rejected as the primary pattern. create_all + trigger fixture: duplicates DDL outside migrations and tests a schema nobody ships. In-memory :memory: SQLite: cannot be shared across connections/sessions the way the app's engine needs, and cannot be template-copied. One shared DB with truncation between tests: ordering-sensitive and slow on Postgres.",
        "risks": "Session-scoped template means schema changes require fixture cache invalidation — the template path embeds the Alembic head revision in its filename, so a new revision automatically rebuilds. Per-test PG database creation is slower (~100ms each) — confined to the small pg-marked subset. Raw-SQL bypass tests are tightly coupled to trigger names/tokens — intentional pinning; they exist to fail when guards change."
      },
      {
        "title": "Seed-data architecture (deterministic, per-template, three months of linked transactions)",
        "decision": "backend/seed.py is a CLI (argparse: --templates defaulting to all five industry templates, --anchor-date defaulting to today, --reset) that assumes a migrated database (Makefile target chains alembic upgrade head). Determinism: one `random.Random(f'{template}:{anchor_date}')` per tenant — identical output for a given (template, anchor) pair; the anchor is recorded on the tenant so reruns are reproducible for bug reports. Provisioning phase under system_context(): per template, create tenant (slug demo-<template>, fixed admin credentials sourced from .env.example values), apply the YAML industry template via the industry module's real application service — modules toggled, display labels, chart-of-accounts preset, tax codes, number-sequence patterns, system roles, custom-field defs (written through core/custom_fields.py). Transaction phase: set the tenancy ContextVar to the tenant (NOT system_context — business writes must be stamped and filtered normally) and drive everything through the REAL service layer wrapped in run_in_uow(), never raw inserts — so numbering, docflow registration and links, domain events (goods issue → COGS), audit rows, and DB triggers all fire exactly as in production, making seed a standing integration proof. Script per template spans 3 calendar months ending at anchor: master data first (items, vendors, customers, warehouses, employees, WBS elements, exchange rates including one foreign currency); then interlinked flows — procurement P2P chains (requisition → PO → goods receipt → AP invoice → payment run), sales O2C (quote → order → delivery → customer invoice → receipt, including partial shipments and one open backorder), template-specific depth (production orders with WIP postings for manufacturing; projects + timesheets for professional-services; maintenance orders for construction; quality inspection lots for healthcare/retail receiving), foreign-currency invoices plus a month-end FX revaluation run, manual journal entries, and month-end closes: periods for months 1 and 2 CLOSED via the real period-close service, month 3 left OPEN with open AP/AR items so aging, dunning, and dashboards have live data. Volumes ~100-300 documents per tenant (seconds on SQLite). Idempotency: without --reset, seed refuses if a demo tenant exists; --reset hard-deletes the demo tenants by cascade — the ONLY sanctioned hard-delete path in the codebase, running under system_context and documented as such. Self-verification: seed ends by asserting, per tenant, (a) trial balance debits == credits, (b) every created document's docflow chain traverses end-to-end, (c) inventory GL balance == sum of inv_item_valuations — and CI runs seed against SQLite after the test suite as a smoke gate.",
        "rationale": "Seeding through real services is the load-bearing choice: SQL-dump seeds rot with every migration and bypass exactly the invariants (gapless numbers, docflow, COGS events, period triggers) the demo exists to showcase, while service-driven seeding doubles as an end-to-end integration test the CI runs for free. Deterministic RNG + recorded anchor gives reproducible demos and bug reports without freezing real time. Closing two of three months demonstrates the period-close machinery and leaves believable open items for the operational screens.",
        "alternatives_rejected": "SQL dump / fixtures files: bypass invariants, drift with schema, undebuggable diffs. Faker with random seed-per-run: non-reproducible demo states. Seeding via HTTP API: needs a running server and auth choreography for zero added fidelity — the service layer is the contract. A full year of data: slower seeds for no demo value; the parity scope's reports all read well at 3 months.",
        "risks": "Anchor defaulting to today means runs on different days differ in dates (structure stays identical given anchor) — acceptable; CI pins a fixed anchor for the smoke gate. Seed duration creeps as modules land — bounded by per-tenant volume caps and the CI timing check. The --reset cascade is a footgun if pointed at a non-demo tenant — guarded by a slug prefix check (refuses anything not starting with 'demo-')."
      }
    ]
  }
}
</output>

task.description: Architect panel: derive the ~15 key technical decisions for Atlas ERP core + financial engine
task.output:
{
  "summary": "Architect panel: derive the ~15 key technical decisions for Atlas ERP core + financial engine",
  "agentCount": 3,
  "logs": [],
  "result": {
    "count": 20,
    "decisions": [
      {
        "title": "Tenancy enforcement (non-bypassable session filter)",
        "decision": "Three cooperating layers in core/tenancy.py + core/db.py. (1) Context: ContextVar[uuid.UUID | None] `current_tenant_id`, set only by `get_current_user` in core/deps.py after JWT validation (and by the refresh endpoint directly from the validated refresh-token tenant_id claim — refresh does NOT use system_context), reset via token in a finally block by a pure-ASGI middleware. (2) Read/write filtering: a global `@event.listens_for(Session, \"do_orm_execute\")` hook on the sync Session class (AsyncSession proxies it, so it covers all execute calls and relationship/lazy loads) adds `with_loader_criteria(TenantMixin, lambda cls: cls.tenant_id == current_tenant_id.get(), include_aliases=True, track_closure_variables=False)` to every ORM statement, including ORM-enabled update()/delete(). FAIL-CLOSED: if the statement touches any TenantMixin mapper and `current_tenant_id` is unset, raise TenancyError — unless the `system_context()` ContextVar (also in core/tenancy.py) is active; system_context is invoked in exactly four greppable places: login user-lookup, tenant provisioning in admin, Alembic/seed provisioning phase, and bus system-event replay. (3) Write stamping: a `before_flush` listener stamps tenant_id on new TenantMixin objects when unset and raises TenancyError when a new/dirty object's tenant_id differs from the context. (4) DB backstop: every FK between tenant-scoped tables is composite `(tenant_id, <entity>_id)` referencing `UNIQUE (tenant_id, id)` on the parent, declared via a `tenant_fk()` helper in core/models.py. CRITICAL SQLite fix: SQLite only enforces FKs with `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`, so core/db.py registers an engine `connect` event that emits the pragma on every SQLite connection (runtime, tests, seed) — without this the backstop silently does nothing on the test engine. Core-level statements (Core Table inserts, text()) bypass the ORM hook; they are sanctioned only inside core/ (audit writer, numbering, idempotency) where tenant_id is always explicit, enforced by a CI grep gate banning `text(` and Core `.insert(` under app/modules/ (tests/ is exempt — DB-guard tests need raw SQL). Non-bypassability tests in tests/core/test_tenancy.py iterate `Base.registry.mappers` so new models are auto-covered: for every TenantMixin mapper assert (a) bare select() under tenant A returns zero tenant-B rows, (b) relationship loads never leak, (c) ORM update() with no WHERE touches only tenant-A rows, (d) execution with unset ContextVar raises, (e) inserting a foreign tenant_id raises, (f) session.get(cls, b_id) under tenant A returns None.",
        "rationale": "do_orm_execute + with_loader_criteria is the only SQLAlchemy 2.0 mechanism that injects criteria into every ORM statement — including lazy loads and bulk ORM writes — with zero cooperation from query authors, which is the literal 'cannot bypass' requirement. ContextVar is async-task-safe under FastAPI. Fail-closed converts 'forgot to set tenant' from a leak into a hard error. Composite FKs give a schema-level invariant on both engines, but only if the SQLite FK pragma is actually on — the original draft omitted that, which would have made the backstop a no-op exactly where CI runs. Mapper-enumerating tests make the guarantee self-extending.",
        "alternatives_rejected": "PostgreSQL RLS with SET LOCAL app.tenant_id: unprovable in the SQLite CI/demo run, so it cannot be the primary mechanism; noted in DECISIONS.md as Postgres-only hardening post-v1. Per-query .where() helpers or custom Query base: bypassable by anyone writing select() directly. Schema- or database-per-tenant: contradicts the mandated row-level design and makes provisioning/Alembic disproportionately heavy. Mapper write-events only: guards writes, not reads.",
        "risks": "Raw SQL and Core statements bypass the hook — bounded by the grep gate, the composite-FK backstop, and review; residual gap recorded in DECISIONS.md. Identity-map hits (session.get) skip SQL — benign because the request-scoped session only ever holds same-tenant rows; sessions are never shared across requests. track_closure_variables=False is mandatory so the lambda re-reads the ContextVar per execution instead of baking in the first value seen; a dedicated test executes the same statement under two tenants in one process to pin this."
      },
      {
        "title": "Auth token flow (JWT access+refresh, rotation with grace window, argon2)",
        "decision": "PyJWT, HS256, single `ATLAS_SECRET_KEY` (env, >=64 random bytes). Access token: 15-min TTL, claims {sub: user_id, tenant_id, sid: refresh-session id, ver: user.token_version, typ: 'access', jti, iat, exp}; stateless, but `ver` is compared against core_users.token_version (the user row is loaded anyway for RBAC), so 'revoke everything' = increment token_version. No permissions in the token. Refresh token: JWT, 14-day TTL, claims {sub, tenant_id, sid, typ: 'refresh', jti, exp}, delivered as an httpOnly Secure SameSite=Strict cookie scoped to path /api/v1/auth; the access token is returned in the JSON body and held in SPA memory only. Server state: core_refresh_sessions (id uuid = sid, tenant_id, user_id, current_jti_hash sha256, prev_jti_hash sha256 nullable, rotated_at, issued_at, last_used_at, expires_at, revoked_at nullable, ip, user_agent). Rotation with reuse detection AND a 10-second grace window (promoted from 'later' to v1 because the SPA's multi-tab reality makes benign races routine, see frontend auth decision): POST /api/v1/auth/refresh verifies signature+typ, sets the tenancy ContextVar from the token's tenant_id claim, loads the session row by sid; presented-jti hash == current_jti_hash → rotate via single `UPDATE ... SET prev_jti_hash=current_jti_hash, current_jti_hash=:new, rotated_at=now() WHERE id=:sid AND current_jti_hash=:old` (compare-and-swap; the loser of a true race gets 0 rows, then re-reads and falls into the grace branch); presented-jti == prev_jti_hash AND now()-rotated_at < 10s → benign concurrent refresh: rotate again normally from the current chain; any other mismatch → replay: set revoked_at on the whole session family, 401. Logout revokes the sid row and clears the cookie. Login (POST /api/v1/auth/login, body tenant_slug+email+password) runs under system_context() for tenant+user resolution. Passwords: argon2-cffi PasswordHasher(type=argon2id, time_cost=3, memory_cost=65536, parallelism=4) per RFC 9106, executed via anyio.to_thread.run_sync; check_needs_rehash() upgrades on successful login. core/deps.py: HTTPBearer scheme → get_current_user decodes, validates typ/exp/ver, sets the tenancy ContextVar, returns a frozen CurrentUser dataclass (user_id, tenant_id, permissions frozenset).",
        "rationale": "HS256 is sufficient for a single-process monolith — no key-distribution problem exists. Short stateless access tokens keep validation DB-free while ver gives an instant global-revoke valve. Hashing the stored jti means a DB leak cannot mint sessions; CAS rotation gives airtight replay detection; the prev_jti grace window is the standard refinement that distinguishes a two-tab race or a lost response from actual token theft — without it, ordinary SPA usage triggers family revocation and forced logouts. Cookie-held refresh + memory-held access is the standard XSS/CSRF compromise. Argon2 at 64 MiB takes tens of ms, so thread offload is mandatory.",
        "alternatives_rejected": "RS256/EdDSA: key-management cost for a consumer that doesn't exist; revisit only if a second service validates tokens. Opaque DB refresh tokens: the constraint specifies JWT access+refresh; JWT also rejects garbage pre-DB. Redis denylist for access revocation: forbidden infrastructure; 15-min exposure + ver bump suffices. localStorage refresh tokens: XSS-exfiltratable. bcrypt: overridden by the argon2 constraint. No-grace strict rotation (original draft): converts routine multi-tab refresh races into family revocations.",
        "risks": "Symmetric key compromise forges any token — env-only storage, never log tokens, short access TTL. The 10s grace window slightly widens the replay-detection blind spot — accepted: an attacker inside 10s of a legitimate rotation still cannot extend the chain invisibly because every rotation updates prev/current atomically and the family dies on the next out-of-chain presentation. SameSite=Strict assumes SPA and API share a site; a split-origin deploy must move to SameSite=None + CSRF token (documented in DECISIONS.md)."
      },
      {
        "title": "RBAC data model, permission dependency, field masking",
        "decision": "Four tables. core_permissions (id, key UNIQUE like 'finance.journal.post', description) — a global code-defined catalog: each module declares keys as constants in its constants.py, a registry in core/rbac.py collects them, and startup sync + seed.py upsert the catalog; permissions are not tenant-editable. core_roles (id, tenant_id, name, description, is_system; UNIQUE(tenant_id, name)) — tenant-scoped, system roles seeded from industry templates at provisioning. core_role_permissions (role_id, permission_id, composite PK). core_user_roles (tenant_id, user_id, role_id, composite PK). Check path: `require_permission(key)` factory in core/rbac.py returns an async dependency depending on get_current_user; effective permissions resolved once per request by one join query (user_roles ⋈ role_permissions ⋈ permissions), memoized in an in-process TTL cache (60 s) keyed (tenant_id, user_id, token_version); missing key → 403 with envelope code 'permission_denied' naming the key. Routers attach per route: `dependencies=[Depends(require_permission(FIN_JOURNAL_POST))]`. The resolved frozenset lands on CurrentUser and in a `current_permissions` ContextVar set by get_current_user. Field-level read masking (HR compensation/IDs): `Masked(tp, permission)` factory in core/schemas.py returning `Annotated[tp | None, WrapSerializer(functools.partial(_mask_serializer, permission))]` — the permission is bound via functools.partial closure (NOT loose Annotated metadata, which a WrapSerializer cannot read); the serializer reads `current_permissions` at serialization time and returns the real value only if the key (e.g. 'hr.employee.read_compensation') is present, else None. Works under response_model serialization without plumbing SerializationInfo.context. Write side: masked fields are excluded from the entity's Update schema and live behind a separate endpoint+schema guarded by the corresponding update permission, so a partial update can never silently null compensation.",
        "rationale": "Tenant-scoped roles over a code-owned catalog satisfies 'RBAC as data' while preventing tenants from inventing keys no code checks. One resolution query + short TTL cache makes per-route checks O(1) without baking stale permissions into JWTs (revocation lands within 60 s, or instantly via token_version bump which changes the cache key). The partial-bound WrapSerializer is idiomatic Pydantic v2, declares the guarding permission on the field itself, and centralizes masking in one core construct. Masking to None keeps response types honest for the TypeScript mirror (field: string | null).",
        "alternatives_rejected": "Permissions embedded in JWT: stale for 15 min and bloats the token; the user row is loaded anyway. Per-tenant permission catalogs: orphan keys nothing enforces. Casbin/oso engines: external DSLs fight 'RBAC as data + service layer owns logic' and complicate the dual-engine story. # Atlas ERP — Architecture

This document is the implementation contract derived from the Phase-2 architecture review. Each section below is a numbered decision (D-007 … D-026), also indexed in [DECISIONS.md](../DECISIONS.md). Implementers must follow these mechanisms exactly — table names, API names, constraint semantics, trigger behavior, and parameter values are normative, not illustrative. ## D-007 — Tenancy enforcement (non-bypassable session filter)

**Decision.**
Three cooperating layers live in `core/tenancy.py` + `core/db.py`:

1. **Context.** A `ContextVar[uuid.UUID | None]` named `current_tenant_id`, set only by `get_current_user` in `core/deps.py` after JWT validation (and by the refresh endpoint directly from the validated refresh-token `tenant_id` claim — refresh does NOT use `system_context`), reset via token in a `finally` block by a pure-ASGI middleware.
2. **Read/write filtering.** A global `@event.listens_for(Session, "do_orm_execute")` hook on the sync `Session` class (`AsyncSession` proxies it, so it covers all execute calls and relationship/lazy loads) adds `with_loader_criteria(TenantMixin, lambda cls: cls.tenant_id == current_tenant_id.get(), include_aliases=True, track_closure_variables=False)` to every ORM statement, including ORM-enabled `update()`/`delete()`. **Fail-closed:** if the statement touches any `TenantMixin` mapper and `current_tenant_id` is unset, raise `TenancyError` — unless the `system_context()` ContextVar (also in `core/tenancy.py`) is active. `system_context` is invoked in exactly four greppable places: login user-lookup, tenant provisioning in admin, Alembic/seed provisioning phase, and bus system-event replay.
3. **Write stamping.** A `before_flush` listener stamps `tenant_id` on new `TenantMixin` objects when unset and raises `TenancyError` when a new/dirty object's `tenant_id` differs from the context.
4. **DB backstop.** Every FK between tenant-scoped tables is composite `(tenant_id, <entity>_id)` referencing `UNIQUE (tenant_id, id)` on the parent, declared via a `tenant_fk()` helper in `core/models.py`. **Critical SQLite fix:** SQLite only enforces FKs with `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON`, so `core/db.py` registers an engine `connect` event that emits the pragma on every SQLite connection (runtime, tests, seed) — without this the backstop silently does nothing on the test engine.

"""Async engine and session plumbing.

Every engine the app touches (runtime, tests, migrations) is built via build_engine
or has enable_sqlite_foreign_keys attached, so the SQLite FK pragma backstop of
D-007 can never be silently absent.
"""

from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from typing import Any

from sqlalchemy import Engine, event
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import (
    AsyncEngine,
    AsyncSession,
    async_sessionmaker,
    create_async_engine,
)

from app.core.config import get_settings


def _set_sqlite_fk_pragma(dbapi_connection: Any, connection_record: Any) -> None:
    cursor = dbapi_connection.cursor()
    cursor.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
    cursor.close()


def enable_sqlite_foreign_keys(engine: Engine) -> None:
    """SQLite enforces FK constraints only with this per-connection pragma (D-007)."""
    if engine.dialect.name == "sqlite":
        event.listen(engine, "connect", _set_sqlite_fk_pragma)


def build_engine(url: str, **kwargs: Any) -> AsyncEngine:
    """The single sanctioned way to create an engine; attaches the FK pragma listener."""
    engine = create_async_engine(url, **kwargs)
    enable_sqlite_foreign_keys(engine.sync_engine)
    return engine


def build_session_factory(engine: AsyncEngine) -> async_sessionmaker[AsyncSession]:
    return async_sessionmaker(engine, expire_on_commit=False)


engine = build_engine(get_settings().database_url)
session_factory = build_session_factory(engine)


async def get_session() -> AsyncIterator[AsyncSession]:
    """FastAPI dependency. Commits belong to the unit-of-work helper (later task);
    here: yield, roll back on exception, always close via the context manager."""
    async with session_factory() as session:
        try:
            yield session
        except Exception:
            await session.rollback()
            raise

"""Shared fixtures — D-025 template-copy isolation: one migrated SQLite template per
session, copied per test, so real commits are allowed and nothing leaks across tests."""

import shutil
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator, Callable
from pathlib import Path

import pytest
from alembic import command
from alembic.config import Config
from alembic.script import ScriptDirectory
from fastapi import FastAPI
from httpx import ASGITransport, AsyncClient
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncEngine, AsyncSession

from app.core.db import build_engine, build_session_factory, get_session
from app.main import create_app

BACKEND_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def make_alembic_config() -> Callable[[str], Config]:
    def _make(database_url: str) -> Config:
        config = Config(str(BACKEND_DIR / "alembic.ini"))
        # config.attributes outranks ATLAS_DATABASE_URL in env.py, so a developer's
        # shell environment can never redirect test migrations.
        config.attributes["sqlalchemy_url"] = database_url
        return config

    return _make


@pytest.fixture(scope="session")
def template_db_path(
    tmp_path_factory: pytest.TempPathFactory,
    make_alembic_config: Callable[[str], Config],
) -> Path:
    """Build ONE migrated template database for the whole session. The Alembic head
    revision is embedded in the filename so a new migration changes the template
    identity automatically (D-025)."""
    script_dir = ScriptDirectory.from_config(make_alembic_config("sqlite+aiosqlite://"))
    head = script_dir.get_current_head()
    path = tmp_path_factory.mktemp("template") / f"template_{head}.sqlite"
    # Sync session-scoped fixture: env.py's asyncio.run works (no running loop here).
    command.upgrade(make_alembic_config(f"sqlite+aiosqlite:///{path}"), "head")
    return path


@pytest.fixture
async def db_engine(template_db_path: Path, tmp_path: Path) -> AsyncIterator[AsyncEngine]:
    db_path = tmp_path / "test.sqlite"
    shutil.copy(template_db_path, db_path)
    engine = build_engine(f"sqlite+aiosqlite:///{db_path}")
    try:
        yield engine
    finally:
        await engine.dispose()


@pytest.fixture
async def db_session(db_engine: AsyncEngine) -> AsyncIterator[AsyncSession]:
    async with build_session_factory(db_engine)() as session:
        yield session


@pytest.fixture
def app(db_engine: AsyncEngine) -> FastAPI:
    application = create_app()
    factory = build_session_factory(db_engine)

    async def _override_get_session() -> AsyncIterator[AsyncSession]:
        async with factory() as session:
            try:
                yield session
            except Exception:
                await session.rollback()
                raise

    application.dependency_overrides[get_session] = _override_get_session
    return application


@pytest.fixture
async def client(app: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[AsyncClient]:
    transport = ASGITransport(app=app)
    async with AsyncClient(transport=transport, base_url="http://test") as test_client:
        yield test_client

First code PR: the backend skeleton every later module builds on. FastAPI app factory with a uniform error envelope and request-id middleware, async SQLAlchemy engine/session plumbing, declarative Base with the migration-safe naming convention, async Alembic with an empty baseline revision, the template-copy test harness, and the Makefile + docker-compose (db + backend) per D-006.

## Design notes

- \`build_engine()\` is the single sanctioned engine constructor; it attaches the SQLite \`PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON\` listener so the D-007 composite-FK backstop can never be silently absent — including under tests and migrations (env.py routes through the same helper).
- Test isolation per D-025: one migrated template SQLite file per session (Alembic head revision embedded in its filename for automatic invalidation), \`shutil.copy\` per test, real commits allowed.
- Alembic env.py URL precedence: \`config.attributes\` → \`ATLAS_DATABASE_URL\` → ini, so test fixtures pin their URL and a developer's shell env can't redirect test migrations.
- \`Page[T]\` envelope shape only; cursor mechanics arrive with PLAN 3.8 (D-014).
- Catch-all 500 handler sets X-Request-ID from scope state because it runs outside the request-id middleware where the ContextVar is already reset.

## Invariants enforced

- Every error response (AtlasError, validation, HTTPException, unhandled) renders the one \`{error: {code, message, details, request_id}}\` envelope — D-014.
- SQLite FK enforcement pragma on every connection of every engine — D-007 backstop precondition.
- Migrations are the only schema source; tests run against the migrated schema, never \`create_all\` — D-022/D-025.

## Tests

7 passing: health + request-id header, envelope shape for AtlasError/404/validation/500 paths, migration upgrade on fresh DB + FK pragma verification. This PR also flips the CI \`backend\` job from skip-mode to real (uv sync --frozen, ruff, pytest).

## Linked items

Refs PLAN 3.1.

## Out of scope

- Tenancy/auth/RBAC/audit/events/docflow/numbering — PLAN 3.2–3.8, next PRs.
- Postgres CI step — lands with the first pg-marked tests (D-022).
- Frontend service in docker-compose — Phase 15." && sleep 15 && gh pr checks 4 --watch --interval 15

- `backend/app/core/models.py` — `UuidPKMixin`, `TenantMixin` (declared_attr, `sa.Uuid`, not-null, indexed), `tenant_fk()`, `tenant_unique()`, `JSON_VARIANT` (JSONB variant lives in models so migrations import it, per D-022 item 3).

- `backend/tests/conftest.py` — `tenant_a`/`tenant_b` fixtures creating Tenant rows under `system_context` and yielding ids.

Spec items (a)–(i) all covered; extras: `session.get` cross-tenant returns None, accessor fail-closed test, helper-construction tests, and the **D-007 grep gate as a pytest test** (bans `text(`/`.insert(` under `app/modules/`, regex word-bounded so `tenant_context(` doesn't false-positive). ## Deviations (one-liners)
1. **Lambda form**: D-007's literal `lambda cls: cls.tenant_id == current_tenant_id.get()` raises `InvalidRequestError` in SQLAlchemy 2.0.50 (lambda-SQL forbids invoking callables inside the lambda); the ContextVar is read in the per-execution listener and closed over with `track_closure_variables=False` — identical semantics, pinned by test (f).
2. **`tenant_fk` signature**: optional second arg — `tenant_fk("adm_tenants")` anchors tenant_id to the root (single-column, since the root has no tenant_id), `tenant_fk(table, local_column)` builds the D-007 composite form (construction-tested now; first real composite use lands with the next tenant-scoped parent/child pair).
3. **Explicit uq name** `uq_adm_tenant_settings_tenant_id_key`: the D-022 convention keys on column 0 only and would collide with any future tenant_id-leading unique (documented in `tenant_unique()`).
4. **Admin module anatomy**: only `__init__.py` + `models.py` created — empty router/service/constants placeholders would violate the no-stubs rule; full STRUCTURE §3 anatomy materializes with PLAN 14.

## D-007 items not implementable now (where they land)
- Production ContextVar setters (`get_current_user` in `core/deps.py`, refresh-endpoint claim path, ASGI middleware token reset) → PLAN 3.3.
- "Relationship loads never leak" test → needs the first relationship between tenant-scoped models (PLAN 3.3 `core_users`/refresh sessions); the mechanism (criteria propagation + listener lazy-load coverage) is already active.
- The four sanctioned `system_context` call sites → PLAN 3.3 (login), 14.2 (provisioning), 16 (seed), 3.6 (event replay); currently docstring-documented only.

"""D-007 tenancy enforcement: context, non-bypassable session filter, write stamping.

Three of the four cooperating D-007 layers live here:
1. Context — the `current_tenant_id` ContextVar (set by core/deps.py after JWT
   validation from PLAN 3.3 on; by `tenant_context()` in tests and seed).
2. Read/write filtering — the `do_orm_execute` listener.
3. Write stamping — the `before_flush` listener.
The fourth layer (composite FKs + the SQLite FK pragma) lives in core/models.py
and core/db.py.
"""

import uuid
from collections.abc import Iterator
from contextlib import contextmanager
from contextvars import ContextVar
from itertools import chain

from sqlalchemy import event
from sqlalchemy.orm import ORMExecuteState, Session, with_loader_criteria

from app.core.exceptions import TenancyError
from app.core.models import TenantMixin

current_tenant_id: ContextVar[uuid.UUID | None] = ContextVar("current_tenant_id", default=None)
_system_context: ContextVar[bool] = ContextVar("system_context", default=False)


def get_current_tenant_id() -> uuid.UUID | None:
    """Active tenant id, fail-closed: raises unless a tenant context is set.
    Returns None only while system_context() is active."""
    tenant_id = current_tenant_id.get()
    if tenant_id is None and not _system_context.get():
        raise TenancyError("No tenant context is active")
    return tenant_id


@contextmanager
def tenant_context(tenant_id: uuid.UUID) -> Iterator[None]:
    """Run the block as one tenant (tests, seed transaction phase; request handling
    sets the ContextVar directly in core/deps.py with middleware reset, per D-007)."""
    token = current_tenant_id.set(tenant_id)
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        current_tenant_id.reset(token)


@contextmanager
def system_context() -> Iterator[None]:
    """Suspend tenant filtering and write stamping for the block.

    Sanctioned in exactly four greppable app call sites (D-007):
    1. login user-lookup (core/auth, PLAN 3.3);
    2. tenant provisioning in modules/admin (PLAN 14.2);
    3. Alembic/seed provisioning phase (seed.py, PLAN 16);
    4. event-bus system-event replay (core/events, PLAN 3.6).
    Test fixtures may also use it (D-025 tenant_factory). Writers under system
    context must set tenant_id explicitly; the composite-FK backstop still applies.
    """
    token = _system_context.set(True)
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        _system_context.reset(token)


def _involves_tenant_scoped_entities(execute_state: ORMExecuteState) -> bool:
    # all_mappers inspects select() column descriptions / mapper entities AND the
    # bind mapper of ORM-enabled update()/delete() — the D-007 involvement rule.
    return any(issubclass(m.class_, TenantMixin) for m in execute_state.all_mappers)


def _filter_tenant_statements(execute_state: ORMExecuteState) -> None:
    """do_orm_execute listener: inject the tenant predicate into every ORM
    select/update/delete; fail-closed when tenant-scoped entities are touched
    without a tenant context."""
    if not execute_state.is_orm_statement:
        # Core statements bypass by design: sanctioned only inside core/ with
        # explicit tenant_id, bounded by the D-007 grep gate.
        return
    if execute_state.is_column_load or execute_state.is_relationship_load:
        # Refresh and lazy loads inherit the criteria propagated from their
        # originating statement; re-injecting here would break attribute refresh.
        return
    if not (execute_state.is_select or execute_state.is_update or execute_state.is_delete):
        return
    if _system_context.get():
        return
    tenant_id = current_tenant_id.get()
    if tenant_id is None:
        if _involves_tenant_scoped_entities(execute_state):
            raise TenancyError("Tenant-scoped statement executed without a tenant context")
        # Statements touching only non-tenant tables (Alembic bookkeeping, the
        # tenants root) legitimately run with no tenant context.
        return
    execute_state.statement = execute_state.statement.options(
        with_loader_criteria(
            TenantMixin,
            # The ContextVar is read above, in this per-execution listener — the
            # lambda-SQL system forbids invoking .get() inside the lambda itself.
            # track_closure_variables=False keeps the closure value out of the
            # statement cache key, so each execution binds the fresh tenant id
            # instead of baking in the first value seen (pinned by a test).
            lambda cls: cls.tenant_id == tenant_id,
            include_aliases=True,
            track_closure_variables=False,
        )
    )


def _stamp_tenant_on_flush(session: Session, flush_context: object, instances: object) -> None:
    """before_flush listener: stamp tenant_id on new tenant-scoped instances and
    reject any new/dirty instance whose tenant_id differs from the context."""
    if _system_context.get():
        # Provisioning/seed/system writes set tenant_id explicitly; the composite
        # FK backstop still rejects ids that do not exist in adm_tenants.
        return
    active = current_tenant_id.get()
    for obj in chain(session.new, session.dirty):
        if not isinstance(obj, TenantMixin):
            continue
        if active is None:
            raise TenancyError("Tenant-scoped instance flushed without a tenant context")
        if obj.tenant_id is None:
            obj.tenant_id = active
        elif obj.tenant_id != active:
            raise TenancyError(
                "Instance tenant_id differs from the active tenant context",
                code="tenancy.tenant_mismatch",
            )


def install_tenancy_guards() -> None:
    """Attach both listeners to the sync Session class — AsyncSession proxies it,
    so every execute call and relationship load is covered. Idempotent so repeated
    calls cannot double-register. Invoked at import time of app.core.db: every
    engine/session factory in app, tests and seed is built from that module, so no
    session can exist unguarded (models.py cannot host the call — this module
    imports TenantMixin from it, which would be an import cycle)."""
    if not event.contains(Session, "do_orm_execute", _filter_tenant_statements):
        event.listen(Session, "do_orm_execute", _filter_tenant_statements)
    if not event.contains(Session, "before_flush", _stamp_tenant_on_flush):
        event.listen(Session, "before_flush", _stamp_tenant_on_flush)

A \`do_orm_execute\` session listener injects the tenant predicate into every ORM select/update/delete and fails closed when a tenant-scoped entity is touched without a tenant context; a \`before_flush\` listener stamps \`tenant_id\` on new rows and rejects cross-tenant writes; composite \`(tenant_id, id)\` foreign keys plus the SQLite FK pragma form the schema-level backstop. Adds the \`adm_tenants\` root table and \`adm_tenant_settings\` (the first real tenant-scoped table) via migration 0002.

## Design notes

- \`install_tenancy_guards()\` is called at import time of \`core/db.py\` — every engine/session factory in app, tests, and seed is built from that module, so no session can exist unguarded. (It can't live in models.py: tenancy imports TenantMixin from there, which would cycle.)
- D-007 literally specifies \`lambda cls: cls.tenant_id == current_tenant_id.get()\`, but invoking \`.get()\` inside a lambda-SQL closure raises \`InvalidRequestError\` in SQLAlchemy 2.0.50. The ContextVar is instead read in the per-execution listener and closed over with \`track_closure_variables=False\` — identical semantics, pinned by the two-tenant-in-one-process test.
- \`system_context()\` suspends filtering for the four sanctioned call sites (login lookup, provisioning, seed, event replay); writers under it set \`tenant_id\` explicitly and the FK backstop still applies.
- The tenancy test class iterates \`Base.registry.mappers\`, so every future \`TenantMixin\` model is auto-covered by the isolation assertions.

## Invariants enforced

- No ORM read or write crosses a tenant boundary; missing tenant context is a hard error, not a silent full-table access (service + DB-FK layers).
- A \`text(\` / Core \`.insert(\` grep gate over \`app/modules/\` is enforced as a pytest test (raw SQL bypasses the ORM hook; sanctioned only inside \`core/\`).

## Tests

25 passing (18 new). Covers: cross-tenant select returns zero rows; ORM update/delete without WHERE touches only the active tenant; unset-context raises; foreign-tenant insert raises; \`system_context\` bypass; same statement under two tenants returns each tenant's rows (closure-variable pin); auto-stamp; composite-FK IntegrityError even under system context (proves PRAGMA + FK); \`session.get\` cross-tenant returns None; mapper-enumeration auto-cover; grep gate.

## Linked items

Refs PLAN 3.2.

## Out of scope

- Production ContextVar setters (\`get_current_user\`, refresh path, middleware reset) — PLAN 3.3.
- Relationship-load leak test — needs the first relationship between two tenant-scoped models (PLAN 3.3); the propagation mechanism is already active.
- PostgreSQL RLS hardening — post-v1 (noted in D-007)." && sleep 15 && gh pr checks 5 --watch --interval 15

async def refresh(
    request: Request,
    response: Response,
    session: SessionDep,
) -> TokenResponse:
    token = request.cookies.get(_COOKIE_NAME)
    if not token:
        raise AuthError(message="Missing refresh token", code="auth.invalid_token")

    claims = auth.decode_token(token, expected_typ="refresh")
    try:
        sid = uuid.UUID(claims["sid"])
        tenant_id = uuid.UUID(claims["tenant_id"])
        user_id = uuid.UUID(claims["sub"])
    except (KeyError, ValueError, TypeError) as exc:
        raise AuthError(message="Invalid refresh token", code="auth.invalid_token") from exc

    # Refresh sets the tenancy ContextVar directly from the validated claim (D-007
    # item 1: refresh does NOT use system_context), so the session loads run scoped.
    current_tenant_id.set(tenant_id)

    sess = await _load_session(session, sid)
    now = auth.now_utc()
    if sess is None or sess.revoked_at is not None or auth.as_utc(sess.expires_at) <= now:
        raise AuthError(message="Invalid refresh token", code="auth.invalid_token")

    presented_hash = auth.sha256_hex(claims["jti"])

    if presented_hash == sess.current_jti_hash:
        return await _rotate(session, sess, user_id, tenant_id, response, now)

    within_grace = (
        sess.prev_jti_hash is not None
        and presented_hash == sess.prev_jti_hash
        and sess.rotated_at is not None
        and (now - auth.as_utc(sess.rotated_at)) < timedelta(seconds=_GRACE_SECONDS)
    )
    if within_grace:
        # Benign concurrent refresh (a second tab raced or a response was lost):
        # rotate again from the CURRENT chain rather than revoking the family.
        return await _rotate(session, sess, user_id, tenant_id, response, now)

    # Any other mismatch is a replay of a stale token: kill the whole session family.
    await _revoke_family(session, sid, now)
    raise AuthError(message="Refresh token reuse detected", code="auth.invalid_token")


async def _rotate(
    session: AsyncSession,
    sess: RefreshSession,
    user_id: uuid.UUID,
    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
    response: Response,
    now: datetime,
) -> TokenResponse:
    """Issue a new token pair and compare-and-swap the session's jti chain. The CAS
    WHERE clause makes a true race deterministic: the loser updates 0 rows and gets a
    401 (it will retry through the grace branch with the prev jti). token_version is
    re-read from the user row so a mid-session global revoke takes effect on refresh."""
    user = (
        await session.execute(select(User).where(User.id == user_id))
    ).scalar_one_or_none()
    if user is None or not user.is_active:
        raise AuthError(message="Invalid refresh token", code="auth.invalid_token")

    sid = sess.id
    body, new_jti = _issue_tokens(response, user_id, tenant_id, sid, user.token_version, now)
    new_hash = auth.sha256_hex(new_jti)
    old_current = sess.current_jti_hash

    result = await session.execute(
        update(RefreshSession)
        .where(RefreshSession.id == sid, RefreshSession.current_jti_hash == old_current)
        .values(
            prev_jti_hash=old_current,
            current_jti_hash=new_hash,
            rotated_at=now,
            last_used_at=now,
        )
    )
    if result.rowcount == 0:
        # Lost a true CAS race: another worker rotated first. Roll back and 401; the
        # client retries and lands in the grace branch on the next attempt.
        await session.rollback()
        raise AuthError(message="Concurrent refresh", code="auth.invalid_token")
    await session.commit()
    return body

Authentication per D-008: argon2id password hashing (off-thread), HS256 access/refresh JWTs, server-side refresh sessions with compare-and-swap rotation, and the \`/api/v1/auth\` endpoints (login, refresh, logout, me). \`get_current_user\` becomes the production setter for the D-007 tenant ContextVar, and request middleware now resets it after every request so a tenant can't leak between requests on a worker.

## Design notes

- **Refresh rotation:** the stored jti is rotated by a conditional \`UPDATE ... WHERE current_jti_hash = :old\` (CAS); the immediately-previous jti is accepted within a 10s grace window (benign multi-tab / lost-response races rotate instead of revoking); any older-token replay revokes the whole session family. A lost CAS race updates 0 rows → 401, and the client retries through the grace branch.
- **Global revoke valve:** access tokens carry \`ver\`, compared to \`core_users.token_version\` (loaded anyway); bumping it invalidates all of a user's access tokens within their 15-min TTL.
- **Token storage:** access token in the JSON body (SPA memory), refresh JWT in an httpOnly Secure SameSite=Strict cookie scoped to \`/api/v1/auth\`.
- **Placement (D-027):** \`User\`/\`RefreshSession\` in \`core/models.py\`, endpoints in \`core/security_router.py\` — auth is cross-cutting platform, not a business module; \`core/auth.py\` stays ORM-free.

## Invariants enforced

- A stolen refresh token is single-use: reuse after rotation is detected and revokes the family (service layer + CAS).
- A request's tenant context comes only from a validated token and is reset after the request (no cross-request leakage).
- Passwords are never stored or compared in plaintext; argon2id at RFC 9106 params, rehash-on-login when params strengthen.

## Tests

51 passing (+20). Covers hash/verify + needs_rehash, JWT round-trip/expiry/wrong-typ/tamper, login happy + bad-password + unknown-tenant 401s, \`me\` with/without token, stale token_version rejection, forged foreign-tenant token rejection (tenant isolation through the user relationship), refresh rotation, out-of-grace reuse → 401 + family revoked, within-grace prev-jti reuse → 200, logout → subsequent refresh 401.

## Linked items

Refs PLAN 3.3. Provides the \`authed_client\` fixture later module tests reuse.

## Out of scope

- RBAC permission resolution — \`get_current_user\` returns an empty permission set with a seam for PLAN 3.4 (D-009); no fake data.
- Trusted-proxy \`X-Forwarded-For\` for session IP — lands with audit (PLAN 3.5)." && sleep 15 && gh pr checks 6 --watch --interval 15

cd "/Users/taha/Claude projects/expremental ERP/atlas-erp" && gh pr create --base dev --title "feat(core): RBAC as data with permission catalog and field masking (D-009)" --label "module:core" --body "## Summary

Role-based access control per D-009. Permissions are code-defined keys (\`module.entity.action\`) synced into a global catalog; roles and their grants are per-tenant data. \`get_current_user\` now resolves a principal's effective permissions (one join, 60s TTL cache) and seeds the \`current_permissions\` ContextVar, filling the seam left by the auth PR. Adds \`require_permission\` route guards and \`Masked()\` field-level read masking.

## Design notes

- **Catalog as source of truth:** tenants can only be granted keys that exist in code — \`create_role\` rejects unknown keys (422 \`rbac.unknown_permission\`), so no tenant can grant a right nothing enforces.
- **\`Permission\` is global** (not tenant-scoped): one row per key describing what the code checks, identical for all tenants. \`Role\`/\`RolePermission\`/\`UserRole\` are tenant-scoped with the composite-FK backstop.
- **Resolution cache** keyed on \`(tenant_id, user_id, token_version)\` with a monotonic clock (override for deterministic tests); \`invalidate\` is called on role assignment, and a token_version bump naturally evicts.
- **Masking** is a real Pydantic v2 \`WrapSerializer\` (permission bound via \`functools.partial\`) that emits \`None\` unless the guarding permission is in the ContextVar; convention is to exclude masked fields from Create/Update schemas (HR enforces for compensation).
- rbac↔deps import cycle broken by a lazy import inside \`require_permission\`.

## Invariants enforced

- No endpoint guarded by \`require_permission(key)\` executes for a principal lacking \`key\` (403, tenant-correct — a grant in tenant A never applies in tenant B).
- A masked field never serializes its real value without the guarding permission present in the request context.

## Tests

74 passing (+14): catalog sync idempotency, unknown-key rejection, union-of-roles resolution, empty set for role-less users, \`require_permission\` 403/200, tenant-correct denial, TTL cache invalidation on assignment, masking on/off via ContextVar + exclusion from Create schema, \`/auth/me\` returns granted permissions.

## Linked items

Refs PLAN 3.4. Completes the get_current_user permissions seam from PR #6.

## Out of scope

- Admin endpoint that bumps \`token_version\` (revoke-now) — PLAN 14.
- Write-side masked-field update guarding — enforced by HR (PLAN 10); convention documented + tested now.
- Industry-template system-role seeding — PLAN 14/16 (\`is_system\` column in place)." && sleep 15 && gh pr checks 7 --watch --interval 15

All tasks complete. Here is the final report.

## PLAN 3.5 — Audit (D-010) complete

**Result:** ruff `check` green, pytest **92 passed** (was 74 → +18: 15 new in `test_audit.py`, +3 from the D-007 mapper-enumeration class auto-covering the new `AuditLog` mapper). No stray `atlas.db`. All files < 400 lines.

### Files created
- `backend/app/core/audit.py` (245) — `RequestContext` + the three context ContextVars (`request_id_ctx`, `actor_user_id_ctx`, `request_ip_ctx`, owned here), `json_safe` helper, split-phase listeners (`before_flush` updates/deletes from attribute history, `after_flush` inserts, `after_flush_postexec` one Core insert), the `do_orm_execute` bulk-write guard, and idempotent `install_audit_guards()`.
- `backend/alembic/versions/0005_audit.py` (118) — `core_audit_log` + per-dialect append-only triggers (PG plpgsql `RAISE EXCEPTION` + `REVOKE UPDATE,DELETE`; SQLite `RAISE(ABORT)`), stable names `trg_core_audit_log_no_update/_no_delete`, downgrade drops both.
- `backend/tests/core/test_audit.py` (252).

### Files changed
- `backend/app/core/models.py` — `AuditMixin` marker (with `__audit_exclude__`), `AuditLog` model; applied `AuditMixin` to User (excludes `password_hash`), Role, RolePermission, UserRole.
- `backend/app/modules/admin/models.py` — `AuditMixin` on Tenant + TenantSetting.
- `backend/app/core/config.py` — `trust_proxy: bool = False`.
- `backend/app/core/exceptions.py` — `DB_GUARD_TOKEN_MAP` + `translate_db_guard_error()`.
- `backend/app/core/db.py` — calls `install_audit_guards()` after `install_tenancy_guards()` (documented order).
- `backend/app/main.py` — middleware seeds/resets `request_ip` (trust-proxy aware `_client_ip`) + `actor_user_id`; re-exports `request_id_var = request_id_ctx`; registered `DBAPIError` → `_handle_db_guard_error`.
- `backend/app/core/deps.py` — `get_current_user` sets `actor_user_id_ctx`.
- `backend/app/core/security_router.py` — login rehash now mutates the loaded User (was a bulk `update(User)`, which the new guard forbids).
- `backend/tests/core/test_auth.py`, `test_tenancy.py` — adapted to the bulk-write guard (see deviations).

### Audited models
User, Role, RolePermission, UserRole, Tenant, TenantSetting. **Excluded (documented):** `AuditLog` (recursion) and `RefreshSession` (high-churn token state).

### ATLAS_ token → envelope map
- `ATLAS_AUDIT_APPEND_ONLY` → **409 / `audit.append_only`** (the one active entry)
- Pre-registered for PLAN 4: `ATLAS_PERIOD_CLOSED`→422 `finance.period_closed`, `ATLAS_POSTED_IMMUTABLE`→422 `finance.entry_immutable`, `ATLAS_UNBALANCED_ENTRY`→422 `finance.journal_unbalanced`.

### Listener order (verified)
`before_flush` listeners fire in registration order; `install_tenancy_guards()` runs first (stamps `tenant_id`), then `install_audit_guards()`. Audit reads `tenant_id` only for UPDATE/DELETE (existing rows already carry it) and for INSERT in `after_flush` (tenancy already stamped), so correctness holds and the order is documented as belt-and-suspenders.

### Deviations (each justified)
1. **AuditLog uses `UuidPKMixin` + `TenantMixin` (NOT NULL tenant_id), not D-010's literal `bigint id` / NULLABLE tenant_id / `source` column.** — Binding PLAN 3.5 spec overrides D-010's schema text; TenantMixin gives tenant-isolated reads through the existing D-007 filter for free (the task's isolation test). The Core writer sets `tenant_id` explicitly since it bypasses ORM stamping.
2. **`ATLAS_AUDIT_APPEND_ONLY` → 409, not D-014's 500.** — PLAN 3.5 binds it to `audit.append_only` 409 (a client-visible conflict).
3. **`Tenant` is audited but is not `TenantMixin`** (no `tenant_id`) — `_make_row` scopes its audit rows to the tenant's own PK (it is its own tenant scope).
4. **`security_router.login` rehash + `test_auth.py` token-version bump switched from ORM bulk `update(User)` to loaded-object mutation** — required by the new bulk-write guard; matches D-010's v1 "mutate auditable entities via loaded objects" policy.
5. **The two D-007 bulk-update/delete tenancy tests retargeted from `TenantSetting` (now audited) to `RefreshSession` (non-audited TenantMixin)** — preserves the D-007 narrowing guarantee on a model where bulk writes are still allowed; audited-model bulk writes are now proven-rejected in `test_audit.py`.
6. **DB-guard token map kept in `exceptions.py`** (not a new `core/db_errors.py`) — small dict, STRUCTURE §8.1 prefers extending an existing home.
7. **Migration index line-collapse** by `ruff format` on the new migration only (CI runs `ruff check`, not `format`; left neighboring files untouched to avoid churn).

### Deferred D-010 elements
- **Audit-viewer compensation masking** ("HR compensation captured but masked by the audit viewer") — deferred to the HR module / admin audit-read endpoint (PLAN 10 / 14), since no audit read endpoint exists yet.
- **`pg` marker on the append-only test** for the dual-engine CI matrix (D-022 step B) — the test asserts the token at DB level and runs on SQLite; adding the Postgres `-m pg` marker belongs with the CI matrix wiring (PLAN later / D-022 task), not this slice.

- `backend/tests/core/test_audit.py` (252).

### Files changed
- `backend/app/core/models.py` — `AuditMixin` marker (with `__audit_exclude__`), `AuditLog` model; applied `AuditMixin` to User (excludes `password_hash`), Role, RolePermission, UserRole.

- `backend/app/core/config.py` — `trust_proxy: bool = False`.
- `backend/app/core/exceptions.py` — `DB_GUARD_TOKEN_MAP` + `translate_db_guard_error()`.
- `backend/app/core/db.py` — calls `install_audit_guards()` after `install_tenancy_guards()` (documented order).
- `backend/app/main.py` — middleware seeds/resets `request_ip` (trust-proxy aware `_client_ip`) + `actor_user_id`; re-exports `request_id_var = request_id_ctx`; registered `DBAPIError` → `_handle_db_guard_error`.
- `backend/app/core/deps.py` — `get_current_user` sets `actor_user_id_ctx`.
- `backend/app/core/security_router.py` — login rehash now mutates the loaded User (was a bulk `update(User)`, which the new guard forbids).
- `backend/tests/core/test_auth.py`, `test_tenancy.py` — adapted to the bulk-write guard (see deviations).

### Audited models
User, Role, RolePermission, UserRole, Tenant, TenantSetting. **Excluded (documented):** `AuditLog` (recursion) and `RefreshSession` (high-churn token state).

### ATLAS_ token → envelope map
- `ATLAS_AUDIT_APPEND_ONLY` → **409 / `audit.append_only`** (the one active entry)
- Pre-registered for PLAN 4: `ATLAS_PERIOD_CLOSED`→422 `finance.period_closed`, `ATLAS_POSTED_IMMUTABLE`→422 `finance.entry_immutable`, `ATLAS_UNBALANCED_ENTRY`→422 `finance.journal_unbalanced`.

### Listener order (verified)
`before_flush` listeners fire in registration order; `install_tenancy_guards()` runs first (stamps `tenant_id`), then `install_audit_guards()`. Audit reads `tenant_id` only for UPDATE/DELETE (existing rows already carry it) and for INSERT in `after_flush` (tenancy already stamped), so correctness holds and the order is documented as belt-and-suspenders.

1. **AuditLog uses `UuidPKMixin` + `TenantMixin` (NOT NULL tenant_id), not D-010's literal `bigint id` / NULLABLE tenant_id / `source` column.** — Binding PLAN 3.5 spec overrides D-010's schema text; TenantMixin gives tenant-isolated reads through the existing D-007 filter for free (the task's isolation test). ## Design notes

- **Split-phase capture:** \`before_flush\` diffs updates/deletes from attribute history, \`after_flush\` records insert PKs (now generated), and \`after_flush_postexec\` writes one Core insert per change — a Core insert so it can't recurse into the ORM flush listeners. - **Append-only** is enforced at the DB by per-dialect \`BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE\` triggers raising \`ATLAS_AUDIT_APPEND_ONLY\` (Postgres plpgsql + REVOKE; SQLite \`RAISE(ABORT)\`). A table-driven translator maps that token (and the pre-registered finance tokens) to envelope codes, so DB backstops surface like service errors (D-014).

- **Listener order:** tenancy stamps \`tenant_id\` in \`before_flush\` before audit reads it; audit guards register after tenancy guards.

## Invariants enforced

- Audit rows cannot be modified or deleted (DB triggers).

- **Created** `backend/app/core/events.py` (245 lines) — the bus.
- **Created** `backend/tests/core/test_events.py` (332 lines) — 11 tests.

- Total: **103 passed** (was 92) → **11 new** tests in `test_events.py`.

## Public API signatures

```python
# Base event (frozen Pydantic v2). Subclass declares key as ClassVar + payload fields:
class DomainEvent(BaseModel):           # model_config frozen=True
    key: ClassVar[str] = ""
    tenant_id: uuid.UUID
    occurred_at: datetime               # default_factory utcnow

# Publish (buffers into session.info['pending_events'], NO dispatch):
def publish(session: AsyncSession, event: DomainEvent) -> None
class InProcessEventBus: def publish(self, session, event) -> None
bus: EventBus = InProcessEventBus()     # module singleton, swap point

# Subscription registry:
Handler = Callable[[AsyncSession, DomainEvent], Awaitable[None]]
def subscribe(event_key: str, handler: Handler) -> None
def on(event_type: type[DomainEvent]) -> Callable[[Handler], Handler]   # @on(EventClass)
def handlers_for(event_key: str) -> tuple[Handler, ...]
def clear_subscriptions() -> None
def subscriptions_snapshot() -> dict[str, list[Handler]]
def restore_subscriptions(snapshot) -> None

# Unit-of-work drain point (work may be a coroutine OR a zero-arg async callable):
async def run_in_uow(session: AsyncSession,
                     work: Callable[[], Awaitable[None]] | Awaitable[None]) -> None

# Swap contract + cascade guard:
@runtime_checkable class EventBus(Protocol): def publish(self, session, event) -> None
class EventCycleError(AtlasError)           # code "events.cycle_detected", 500
```

`run_in_uow` sequence: run `work` → drain buffer FIFO and run handlers on the **same** session → `commit`; any exception (work or handler) or cap breach → `rollback` + re-raise, clearing the buffer.

## Cascade cap value

**`MAX_DISPATCHES_PER_UOW = 50`** (total handler dispatches per transaction; exceeding it raises `EventCycleError` and rolls back). The cycle test asserts exactly 50 handlers ran before the raise.

## Ordering guarantee (defined + tested)

Events drain **FIFO** (publish order); within one event key, handlers fire in **registration order** (= module import order in `main.py`'s factory). Cascade events published by handlers drain breadth-first in the same uow. Test asserts `["A:h1","A:h2","B:h1","B:h2"]`.

## Item 2 (audit + tenant stamping) — proven, not reimplemented

`test_handler_write_is_audited_and_tenant_stamped`: a handler inserts a `TenantSetting` with `tenant_id` left unset; the existing D-007 `before_flush` stamp fills it from the active context and the D-010 listeners write the audit row — assertion confirms one `INSERT` audit row stamped to the trigger tenant. No audit/tenancy code touched.

## Atomicity (the cardinal invariant) — unambiguous

`test_handler_failure_rolls_back_trigger_write`: trigger writes a "stock" `TenantSetting` + publishes; the COGS handler writes its own row then raises. After rollback both **counts are asserted == 0** — the trigger's own write does not persist. Counterpart `test_business_work_failure_...` proves a failure before drain skips handlers and persists nothing.

## Demonstration without a business module

Tests define **local** `DomainEvent` subclasses (`StockIssued`, `OrderConfirmed`) + handlers and run against the real session/db; where handler effects must persist/roll back, the existing audited tenant-scoped `adm_tenant_settings` (`TenantSetting`) stands in for a business row. No fake module added to `app/`.

## Deviations (each one-line justified)

- **`run_in_uow` lives in `core/events.py`, not `core/db.py`** as D-011's prose suggests — keeps the drain logic beside the buffer/registry it operates on (one concept per file, STRUCTURE §8.5); `core/deps.py`/`seed.py` will import it from here in their PLAN tasks. No behavioral change.
- **`EventCycleError` is 500, code `events.cycle_detected`** — D-011 names the error but not a code/status; a publish cycle is a server-side wiring fault, so 500 (consistent with the `AtlasError` envelope), and like any handler failure it rolls back.
- **Added free functions `publish`/`handlers_for`/`subscriptions_snapshot`/`restore_subscriptions`** beyond D-011's literal list — convenience/test-isolation surface only; the Protocol method set is unchanged.

## Deferred D-011 elements (and to which PLAN task)

- **Wiring `run_in_uow` into the request session dependency (`core/deps.py`) and seed/CLI flows** — deferred; those modules consume the helper when they exist (deps already exists but has no UoW commit path yet; this lands when the first service needs it, PLAN 4 / the deps UoW task).
- **`core_event_outbox` table + `TransactionalOutboxBus`** — explicitly post-v1 per D-011; the `EventBus` Protocol is the seam, table introduced in a later PLAN task, not now.
- **After-commit hook for non-transactional side effects (email/webhooks)** — D-011 records it as a later seam; banned from this bus, not implemented here.

No `git` operations performed (per instructions). PROGRESS.md/PLAN.md checkbox updates were not made — flag if you want those ticked.

async def run_in_uow(
    session: AsyncSession,
    work: Callable[[], Awaitable[None]] | Awaitable[None],
) -> None:
    """The single sanctioned unit-of-work helper (D-011). Used by the request session
    dependency (core/deps), by seed.py and by CLI flows, so HTTP, seed and tests get
    IDENTICAL event semantics.

    Sequence: run ``work`` (the business mutation that publishes events) -> drain the
    buffered events FIFO and run their handlers on the SAME session (so handler effects,
    e.g. a COGS journal, are in the same transaction as the trigger, e.g. the stock
    issue) -> commit. If the business work OR any handler raises (or the cascade cap is
    hit), roll the WHOLE transaction back and re-raise — the trigger's own writes do not
    persist. Handlers run under the trigger's active tenant context (D-007); nothing here
    changes it.

    ``work`` may be a coroutine object or a zero-arg callable returning an awaitable, so
    both ``run_in_uow(session, service_coro)`` and ``run_in_uow(session, lambda: ...)``
    read naturally at call sites.
    """
    try:
        awaitable = work() if callable(work) else work
        await awaitable
        await _drain_and_dispatch(session)
        await session.commit()
    except Exception:
        await session.rollback()
        # Drop any partially drained / leftover buffer so the next uow on this session
        # (tests reuse one session) starts clean.
        session.info.pop(_BUFFER_KEY, None)
        raise

The in-process domain-event bus that decouples modules per D-011. \`publish()\` buffers events on the session; \`run_in_uow()\` runs the business work, drains the buffer FIFO running each handler on the same session, then commits — so cross-module effects are transactionally consistent with their trigger.

## Design notes

- **Collect-then-dispatch, in-transaction:** handlers run before commit and share the session, so a handler's DB writes (e.g. a COGS journal) commit atomically with the trigger's writes (e.g. a stock issue). They also inherit the existing tenancy stamping and audit capture for free (proven by a test, not reimplemented).
- **Atomicity is the cardinal invariant:** if the business work or any handler raises, the whole transaction rolls back and the trigger's own writes do not persist — a goods issue without its COGS posting cannot commit.
- **Cascade handling:** handlers may publish further events, drained in the same uow up to a cap of 50; a deliberate cycle raises \`EventCycleError\`.
- **Ordering:** events drain FIFO; handlers for one key fire in registration (module import) order.
- **Swappable:** the bus sits behind an \`EventBus\` Protocol; a transactional-outbox bus replaces it post-v1 without touching business logic.

## Invariants enforced

- Handler effects are in the same transaction as their trigger; partial cross-module state can never commit.
- Event subscriptions are reset between tests so later modules' handlers don't leak.

- `backend/app/core/models.py` — tail re-export of numbering/docflow so models register on `Base.metadata` (283 lines, under cap)

## Signatures
- `async def claim_number(session, tenant_id, sequence_name, *, on_date: date) -> str`
- `async def get_document_chain(session, tenant_id, document_id) -> DocumentChain` (returns `nodes: list[ChainNode]`, `edges: list[ChainEdge]`)

## SQLite feature support
- **UPDATE...RETURNING: YES** — verified on aiosqlite 0.22.1 / SQLite 3.53 (sync + async paths) and proven by the atomicity + rollback-reuse tests. No fallback used.
- **WITH RECURSIVE: YES** — verified and proven by the bidirectional-chain + diamond tests.

## New core router recorded
`core/docflow_router.py` recorded in DECISIONS.md as a follow-on to D-027 (same "core platform router" precedent as `security_router.py`), wired in `create_app()`.

## Deviations (each one-line justified)
- **Models in concern files, not `models.py`** — moving `NumberSequence`/`Document`/`DocumentLink` into `numbering.py`/`docflow.py` keeps `models.py` under the ~350-line cap; re-exported at the tail of `models.py` so they still register on `Base.metadata` (the PLAN sanctions this; STRUCTURE §2 lists both files).
- **Route path `/api/v1/documents/{id}/chain`** (binding task path) vs D-012 draft's `/api/v1/core/documents/{id}/flow` — chain shape identical.
- **Sequence schema keyed on `(tenant_id, name)` with `year_reset`/`current_year`** (binding task column spec) vs D-012 draft's `(tenant_id, doc_type, year)` PK — gapless-claim/partial-index/recursive-CTE semantics unchanged.
- **Chain endpoint guarded by `get_current_user` only** (task spec) — the seeded `core.document.read` permission stays available for finer per-doc-type gating in later module work; using it now would 403 the non-admin `authed_client` the task requires for the endpoint test.
- **Two `core_doc_links`→`core_documents` composite FKs given explicit distinct names** — the D-022 column-0 naming convention would name both identically (collision); both names match the migration exactly.

## D-012 elements deferred
- **`docflow.assign_number` / `docflow.set_status`** (post-creation numbering + status mutation in the posting transaction) — deferred to PLAN 4 (finance), where journal-entry posting first needs them; the primitives they compose (`claim_number`, the registry row) are all in place now.
- **Per-doc_type summary callbacks** for display extras — deferred to the finance/module phases that register them.
- **Idempotency-key infrastructure (D-013) and cursor pagination (D-014)** — explicitly the remaining halves of PLAN 3.8, not in this task's scope.

async def claim_number(
    session: AsyncSession,
    tenant_id: uuid.UUID,
    sequence_name: str,
    *,
    on_date: date,
) -> str:
    """Atomically claim the next number for ``sequence_name`` and return the formatted
    string (D-012). The claim runs in the CALLER's transaction — the number is permanent
    only when that transaction commits, so a rollback returns the value to the pool and the
    next committed claim reuses it (gaplessness for committed documents).

    Mechanism — one portable atomic statement per claim:
    ``UPDATE core_number_sequences SET next_value = next_value + 1
      WHERE tenant_id=:t AND name=:n RETURNING next_value`` — the RETURNING value is the
    post-increment counter; the row lock the UPDATE takes serializes concurrent claimers so
    two claims can never read the same number (verified on aiosqlite >= 3.35 and Postgres).

    Year reset (when ``year_reset``): if ``on_date.year`` differs from the stored
    ``current_year``, the counter is reset to 1 for the new year FIRST (a guarded UPDATE
    that only fires while current_year is still the old value, so a concurrent claimer that
    reset it already cannot double-reset), then the normal atomic increment claims 1.

    A Core UPDATE is used (bypasses the ORM tenant filter by design — core/ numbering is a
    D-007 sanctioned raw-SQL site with explicit tenant_id)."""
    sequence = (
        await session.execute(
            select(NumberSequence).where(
                NumberSequence.tenant_id == tenant_id, NumberSequence.name == sequence_name
            )
        )
    ).scalar_one_or_none()
    if sequence is None:
        raise NotFoundError(
            message=f"Number sequence '{sequence_name}' is not configured for this tenant",
            code="core.number_sequence_missing",
        )

    table = NumberSequence.__table__
    claim_year: int | None = None
    if sequence.year_reset:
        claim_year = on_date.year
        if sequence.current_year != claim_year:
            # Reset to 1 for the new year, guarded on the OLD current_year so a racing
            # claimer that already rolled the year over does not reset a second time.
            await session.execute(
                sa.update(table)
                .where(
                    table.c.tenant_id == tenant_id,
                    table.c.name == sequence_name,
                    table.c.current_year.is_not_distinct_from(sequence.current_year),
                )
                .values(next_value=1, current_year=claim_year)
            )

    result = await session.execute(
        sa.update(table)
        .where(table.c.tenant_id == tenant_id, table.c.name == sequence_name)
        .values(next_value=table.c.next_value + 1)
        .returning(table.c.next_value)
    )
    next_after = result.scalar_one()
    claimed_value = next_after - 1

    # The Core UPDATE changed the row out from under the loaded ORM object; expire it so its
    # attributes reload from the DB on next access rather than being marked dirty (which
    # would trigger a redundant ORM UPDATE on the next flush).
    formatted = _format_number(sequence.prefix, sequence.padding, claimed_value, claim_year)
    session.expire(sequence)
    return formatted

Every business document registers in core_documents and links to its
predecessors/successors in core_doc_links; get_document_chain walks both
directions with one recursive CTE so the full chain (requisition -> PO ->
receipt -> invoice) renders from any node, exposed at
GET /api/v1/documents/{id}/chain. Per-tenant numbers are claimed by an
atomic UPDATE ... RETURNING inside the caller's transaction, so a number
becomes permanent only when its document commits and a rollback returns
it to the pool — gaplessness for committed documents falls out of ACID.
A partial unique index keeps doc numbers unique per tenant while many
drafts stay NULL. UPDATE...RETURNING and WITH RECURSIVE both verified on
the project's aiosqlite. core/docflow_router.py recorded under D-027.
Refs PLAN 3.7, PLAN 3.8 (numbering)" && git push -q -u origin feat/core-docflow && gh pr create --base dev --title "feat(core): document registry, flow links, and gapless numbering (D-012)" --label "module:core" --body "## Summary

Implements the document-flow and numbering platform per D-012 (merged). A central \`core_documents\` registry plus \`core_doc_links\` edges let any business document trace its full predecessor/successor chain; per-tenant document numbers (INV-2026-00001) are claimed atomically inside the committing transaction so they're effectively gapless for committed documents. Adds \`GET /api/v1/documents/{id}/chain\`.

## Design notes

- **Gaplessness from ACID:** \`claim_number\` runs one \`UPDATE core_number_sequences SET next_value = next_value + 1 ... RETURNING next_value\` in the caller's transaction; the row lock serializes concurrent claimers, and a rollback returns the value to the pool so the next committed claim reuses it. Year-reset is a guarded update keyed on the old \`current_year\` so a racing claimer can't double-reset.
- **Chain traversal:** \`get_document_chain\` uses recursive CTEs in both directions with a depth cap and a visited-path guard, so diamonds/shared predecessors don't loop. Both \`UPDATE...RETURNING\` and \`WITH RECURSIVE\` were verified on the project's aiosqlite (no fallback needed).
- **Partial unique index** on \`(tenant_id, doc_number) WHERE doc_number IS NOT NULL\` (via \`postgresql_where\` + \`sqlite_where\`) — many drafts stay NULL, numbered docs stay unique per tenant.
- **Placement:** numbering/docflow ORM models live in their concern files (re-exported so they register on \`Base.metadata\`) to keep \`models.py\` under the size cap; the chain router joins \`security_router.py\` as a sanctioned core router (recorded under D-027).

## Invariants enforced

- A committed document's number is unique within its tenant and sequence; concurrent claims never collide.
- Document chains and numbering are tenant-isolated.

## Tests

134 passing (+22): sequential + padded + year-segment claims, year reset, no-duplicate across many/concurrent claims, rollback-reuse gaplessness, per-tenant independent counters, idempotent \`ensure_sequence\`; document registration uniqueness, edge creation + dedup, bidirectional 4-doc chain from a middle node, diamond without infinite loop, partial-unique-index conflict (and cross-tenant reuse allowed), chain tenant isolation, and the authed chain endpoint.

## Linked items

Refs PLAN 3.7 and the numbering half of PLAN 3.8.

## Out of scope

- \`assign_number\`/\`set_status\` posting-transaction helpers — compose the primitives here; land with finance (PLAN 4).
- Idempotency keys (D-013) and cursor pagination (D-014) — the remaining halves of PLAN 3.8, next PR." && sleep 15 && gh pr checks 10 --watch --interval 15

async def test_business_failure_cleans_up_reservation_and_creates_no_document(
    db_engine: AsyncEngine, db_session: AsyncSession, tenant_a: uuid.UUID
) -> None:
    # Fail-closed (D-013): if the business work raises after reserve, the IN_PROGRESS reservation
    # is deleted (not left as COMPLETED) and the document is not created, so the key can be retried.
    app = _build_app(db_engine, tenant_a, fail=True)
    async with await _client(app, raise_app_exceptions=False) as client:
        response = await client.post(
            "/api/v1/_test/settings",
            headers={"Idempotency-Key": "k"},
            json={"key": "theme", "value": {"mode": "dark"}},
        )
    assert response.status_code == 500
    assert response.json()["error"]["code"] == "common.internal_error"
    assert await _load_key(db_session, tenant_a, "k") is None
    assert await _count_settings(db_session, tenant_a) == 0

    # The same key is now free: a fresh (non-failing) handler completes it.
    ok_app = _build_app(db_engine, tenant_a)
    async with await _client(ok_app) as client:
        retry = await client.post(
            "/api/v1/_test/settings",
            headers={"Idempotency-Key": "k"},
            json={"key": "theme", "value": {"mode": "dark"}},
        )
    assert retry.status_code == 201
    row = await _load_key(db_session, tenant_a, "k")
    assert row is not None and row.status == STATUS_COMPLETED
